strengths: One resolver behind both doors: the Stage 6 panel and the Tamper tile end in the same attemptCleanup / resolveCleanup, the door a packet's claim that only swaps one guard for another (scripts/cleanup.mjs:28-58, 1102-1107).

A price a packet says was paid comes back only as far as the GMs' credit holds it, on every road that gives anything back - a refusal, a critical, the free attempt (scripts/cleanup.mjs:2354-2367, paidBack).

The clean-up receipt is a GM store written before the attempt changes anything and counts only the attempt's own Sanity writes, so a Reroll survives an F5 and takes back no one else's marks (scripts/cleanup.mjs:1178-1193, 2233-2245; scripts/cleanup-reshape.mjs:45-68).
A reshape is a proposal: the words are kept on the attempt's row before the card exists and one synchronous claim rules it once, on the primary (scripts/cleanup-reshape.mjs:492-494, 565-579).
A player's words are cut at the boundary (tags, both angle brackets, runs, length) and escaped again where printed (scripts/cleanup-reshape.mjs:292-305, 397-399).
A player's Remnant packet is rebuilt from what the GM knows - who, where, Faint, tie, what it points at - and only band, action and words are taken from it (scripts/remnants.mjs:882-913).

The answer key is off the tokens: a token carries isRemnant and, while its incident runs, fromIncident; remnantData answers null on any browser that is not a GM's (scripts/remnants.mjs:551-556, 1930-1947).
One read of traces: every reader goes through a frozen ref built from the token and its row, and a row with no token is no ref (scripts/remnants.mjs:3207-3245).
The tie's three states and its wait for a death nobody has found are written and read through one pair of functions (scripts/remnants.mjs:1912-1914, 2394-2402, 2412-2416).
setRemnantPublic writes only the fields its caller named and sends the copies only what actually changed (scripts/remnants.mjs:1438-1457).
migrateRemnantToken reads the row back from storage before it strips anything from a token (scripts/remnants.mjs:2954-2962).

Rings, icons and names are drawn on each browser from what that browser may know; no document write, and a ring is kept while its frame key stands (scripts/remnant-ring.mjs:682-706; scripts/remnant-icons.mjs:169-192).

The Key fee is one rule, counted over the items the GMs hold after one wait, held when an answer key is missing, and charged on the primary whichever GM opened the trial (scripts/key-remnants.mjs:626-652, 720-727, 777-780).
setKeyPlan writes a slot's field only when it differs from what the window was drawn from, so two GMs' saves do not take each other back (scripts/key-remnants.mjs:193-216).
A failed cover roll is told to the owners of the witnesses in the room and the GMs, not the table (scripts/cleanup.mjs:1444-1467).
The body's reach is one function for the picker and the resolver, and the packet's room is held to it (scripts/cleanup.mjs:2723-2748, 1956-1958).

No function over 300 lines in the seven files, measured by espree over 511 functions; the four of 150-300 are placeRemnant (scripts/remnants.mjs:331, 262 lines), undoLastCleanup (scripts/cleanup.mjs:2082, 189), attemptCleanup (scripts/cleanup.mjs:559, 173) and resolveCleanup (scripts/cleanup.mjs:1082, 171).

findings.title: The GM scores a clean-up 3 lower for a body the roller's player may not know: the 1.2.110 V3 filter is skipped on the scoring road
findings.where: scripts/cleanup.mjs:811 and 1169-1172 (the verdict is scored with `held`); scripts/cleanup.mjs:451-453 (the filter asks `actor.testUserPermission`); scripts/sheet-audit.mjs:872-875 (`actorHeldNow` answers id, name, type and items only)
findings.what_happens: resolveCleanup scores the attempt with cleanupVerdict(held, ...), where `held` is sheet-audit.mjs actorAsHeld's stand-in: a plain object with id, name, type and items. cleanupVerdict calls cleanupDc(data.visibility, held), which calls freshSceneBonus({ actor: held }) and so unfoundBodyIn(chapter, undefined, held). There `actor.testUserPermission?.(user, "OWNER")` is undefined for every user, `players` is empty, and the GM counts its whole deaths store - the branch written for a character no player owns. The roller's own browser (the briefing, the list's `dc` from cleanableTracesForPlayer, the roll window) reads only the deaths that user may know, so with a body of this chapter unfound and unknown to the roller the window says N and the GM scores against N - 3. This is the state the 1.2.110 review's V3 described and commit 8a6d9bd8 was written to close.
findings.failure_scenario: The GM closes a murder at night and nobody has found the body; next morning an uninvolved student Tampers an Evident trace they found: the window says 15, they roll 13, and the card says the Remnant is gone - a hit below the number shown, which tells that player a body of this chapter lies unfound.
findings.expected: One number on both browsers: scripts/cleanup.mjs:442-447 says a GM counts 'only the rows one of that character's players may know, by the same rule the copy is built by, so both browsers read one number', and docs/dev/e101/REVIEW.md V3 (line 222) records that as fixed.
findings.fix_sketch: Score the fresh scene with the actor document (keep `held` for the tool's tier only), or give actorHeldNow the document's testUserPermission; then drive the V3 test through resolveCleanup, not cleanupDc.
findings.refutation_tried: Looked for another caller that scores with the document: cleanupVerdict is the only scorer (cleanup.mjs:800-824) and resolveCleanup its only caller, with `held` since commit 0851a0a1 (E29 fix r2-H20), five weeks before V3. actorHeldNow (sheet-audit.mjs:872-876) builds the same plain object on every GM, primary or not. The incident branch does not hide it: with an incident running both sides give the -3, so the difference exists exactly between an incident's close and the discovery (bodyDiscovery() is false, no murderState). resolveStageSix does not use the fresh scene, so only Erase and Reshape are touched. The roller who does know of the body (the killer, a witness) reads the same number on both sides.
findings.tests_near: Tier 2 '1.2.110 V3 - a Tamper's fresh scene counts on the GM only the unfound bodies its roller's player may know' (scripts/tests-tier2.mjs:103693) and scenario 30-security's 7n' (audit/harness/scenarios/30-security.mjs:3021-3049) both call cleanupDc(visibility, <the actor document>); the test's note calls that 'the scoring's own road', but resolveCleanup hands cleanupDc the held stand-in, so neither reads what is scored. Tier 1 R3950 (scripts/tests-tier1.mjs:60226, 60269) asks freshSceneBonus by arguments and reads cleanupDc's text.
findings.live_check: One GM, one player P whose character is not in the incident: run an incident to a death, close it, do not discover the body, stay out of the Investigation; P Tampers a found trace bare-handed. Compare the roll window's number with 'against DC' on the GMs' Clean-up card: they should be equal.

findings.title: A critical cover roll clears a Sanity mark on the roller's own browser as a refund of nothing: the GMs' audit flags it, or it eats another payment's credit
findings.where: scripts/cleanup.mjs:1420-1421 and 2540-2546 (concealFromWitnesses -> restoreStress, reason "refund"); scripts/config.mjs:4826 (conceal.refundStress.critical: 1); scripts/sheet-audit.mjs:1776-1781 (a refund is covered by credit alone) and 1769-1773 (an uncovered Sanity gain is flagged)
findings.what_happens: With a witness in the room, attemptCleanup and attemptStageSix roll the cover first, on the roller's browser. On a critical the cover costs nothing (cost stays 0) and restoreStress then lowers the roller's Sanity marks by 1 through trustedWrite with reason "refund". On the primary GM a player's refund is covered only by credit a payment left in the last 30 minutes (REFUNDS, coverOf, CREDIT_KEPT_MS = TIMING.rerollWindowMinutes). The cover roll itself paid nothing, so with no recent Sanity payment the gain is uncovered and, with lockPlayerResources on (the default), goes out as a flagged write with Undo and Keep; with a recent payment it silently takes that payment's credit, which a Reroll's give-back of that payment would then find gone. The main roll's critical was moved off this pattern in T-1 and r2-G8 (handBack / paidBack hand back the step that paid, on the GM, as far as the GMs saw it paid); the cover roll's was not.
findings.failure_scenario: A student carrying one Sanity mark since the morning Tampers in front of a classmate and rolls a critical on 'Hide what you are doing': the mark is cleared, and the GMs get a flagged-write card about that student's Sanity with Undo and Keep, for an outcome the module's own table gave.
findings.expected: A legal road raises nothing at the GMs' audit (the repository's trust-model rule file, trust-model.md, layer two; scenario 83's rule), and a give-back hands back what was paid: scripts/cleanup.mjs:2392-2396 records why the main roll stopped clearing 'a Sanity mark the attempt never made'.
findings.fix_sketch: Make the cover roll's give-back on the GM as the main roll's is (with the attempt's packet, through paidBack), or give nothing back where the cover cost nothing.
findings.refutation_tried: Looked for another cover of a refund-stamped gain in sheet-audit.mjs coverOf (1776-1788): REFUNDS take credit and nothing else; `rest`, `itemUse` and `call` are other reasons. gainVerdict (1769-1773) puts Hope back and flags Sanity under the lock, lists it without. settings.mjs:3156 registers lockPlayerResources true. restoreStress writes only when a mark stands (2542), so a roller with no marks is untouched. Whether the critical should clear a mark at all is the table's rule (config.mjs:4826) and is not questioned here; the write's place is. Not run: the road needs a roll forced critical on a player's page.
findings.tests_near: Tier 2 'a Tamper window closed after a landed concealment roll keeps its price ...' (scripts/tests-tier2.mjs:41664) lands a 30 with Hope, not a critical, on the GM's own browser. Scenario 83's L9 (83-roll-integrity.mjs:491-546) cleans up alone, so no cover roll is thrown. 13-murder-signals (687-705) reads the reason on the price's rise only. None drives a critical cover roll from a player's page.
findings.live_check: On the harness or a table: a player's character with 1 Sanity mark older than 30 minutes, a second student in the room; force the cover roll critical; read game.drpg.sheetWrites() and the GMs' chat for a flagged row on system.resources.stress.value.

findings.title: A Tamper's result cards name the trace's real band and category to a roller who holds only an unanalysed copy
findings.where: scripts/cleanup.mjs:954-956 (the erase's line, whispered by report 2580-2592); scripts/cleanup-reshape.mjs:392-400 and 661-665 (the approved reshape's line); scripts/cleanup.mjs:788-790 (the reinforced refusal)
findings.what_happens: Through Tamper's door a trace is listed for a character who holds a copy of it, and since E05 C14 the list labels it by that copy's name and 'by nothing of the ledger' (cleanup.mjs:306-316), because the category is what an Analyze is paid for. The cards that follow the roll still print the ledger's reading: a successful erase whispers the roller 'The {visibilityLabel} {typeLabel} is gone.', an approved reshape whispers '{visibilityLabel} {typeLabel} now reads as ...', and a trace reinforced meanwhile is refused by the same two labels. The roller's own Truth Bullet keeps its answer key through the erase and the reshape, so the card hands them the category of a bullet they have not analysed.
findings.failure_scenario: An investigator who copied a trace and never analysed it erases it with Tamper and reads 'The Subtle Incident Remnant is gone.' - their neutral Truth Bullet is now known to be the incident's, with no Analyze.
findings.expected: Off Stage 6 a trace the character holds a copy of is named by that copy and by nothing of the ledger (scripts/cleanup.mjs:306-316, E05 C14, audit S05-14); Stage 6's killer keeps the whole label.
findings.fix_sketch: For a roller who is not Stage 6's cleaner, word these three lines with the copy's name (copyNamesOf) and keep band and category on the GMs' card.
findings.refutation_tried: Checked who reads the card: whisperToOwner goes to the character's owners and the GMs (utils.mjs:751-758), veiled. Checked that the copy survives: an erase leaves copies (removeRemnant drops the row and the token only) and a reshape passes propagate: false (cleanup-reshape.mjs:390). The band alone is no news (a bullet shows its band, remnant-ring.mjs:482-501); the category is, until shownType leaves 'neutral'. An incident's own trace watched being made keeps its label by the comment's own rule, and a Key or a Final shows its kind on pickup, so the case is a Prep, Faint, Incident or Tamper trace found by somebody who was not in the incident. No owner's decision on the result cards was found in docs/dev, the handbooks or the release notes.

findings.title: keyPlanStatus counts every plan slot as a Key Remnant: 'every planned Key Remnant has been found' never comes for a case of three or four, and the GM's line reads 'N of 5'
findings.where: scripts/key-remnants.mjs:131 (a plan always has at least five entries) and 525-533 (`missing`, and `entries.length` as the total); read by scripts/gm-panel.mjs:921-927, scripts/events.mjs:642-647, scripts/investigation.mjs:924-926
findings.what_happens: keyPlan() answers at least KEY_REMNANTS.scale.length = 5 entries whatever was written, and keyPlanStatus() reports `missing` as every entry not found - a slot nobody wrote and no trace stands on included. An opening on Despair gives a case four Key Remnants and a critical three (config.mjs:3689), and the realization leaves the slots at or past that limit unplaced as 'overLimit' (case-realize.mjs:45). So for such a case `missing` can never reach 0: the GM panel's next step stays 'The Investigation is running...' after the last Key is found, and the GM's body line on the Event card says for example '4 of 5 Key Remnants found' for a case whose four are all found. missingKeyRows in the same file already uses the other rule: a slot with nothing written and no trace is no Key Remnant (key-remnants.mjs:540-541, 555).
findings.failure_scenario: The killer's opening comes up with Despair, the GM places the case's four Key Remnants and the class finds all four: the panel never says 'Every planned Key Remnant has been found. Start the Class Trial', and the Event card tells the GM '4 of 5 Key Remnants found'.
findings.expected: docs/handbooks/gm-handbook.en.md:249: 'once every planned Key Remnant is found, start the Class Trial (Open the trial console)'; the case's own count is caseKeyCount (key-remnants.mjs:398-405).
findings.fix_sketch: Count as planned only the slots inside caseKeyCount that hold a trace or words (missingKeyRows' rule) and report that as the total.
findings.refutation_tried: Checked whether an unused slot can read as found: only a living finder of its trace or Monokuma's Reveal makes `found` (key-remnants.mjs:491-494). Checked whether the panel reaches the branch another way: nextStep's investigation branch has this one test (gm-panel.mjs:912-928). E109's D22 fixed the same miscount for the limit's line only (keyRowsUsed, key-remnants.mjs:153-161). The panel's 'N still to place' line above it is limit-aware (keysToPlace), so only the found side is off. For an opening with Hope and five placed the line does come.
findings.tests_near: None found: git grep for nextStartTrial and bodyMetaGm over scripts/tests*.mjs and audit/harness/scenarios finds nothing; the tier-2 tests that call keyPlanStatus read `found`, `placed` and `offPlan`.

findings.title: A bystander's Misleading Trail aimed at the running incident's victim is refused with 'You cannot frame that student' - a name their own menu offered
findings.where: scripts/cleanup.mjs:1591-1596 (framingCandidates reads this browser's murderState) and 1778-1781 (the GM's refusal); scripts/incident-store.mjs:176-184 (a bystander's cast is {})
findings.what_happens: The Tamper tile's Frame row lists framingCandidates(actor) on the roller's browser: the living students but the roller, a Monokuma and murderState()?.victimId. A bystander's browser holds no cast, so the victim - alive in the opening or the fight, or dead and not yet published in Stage 6 - is on the list. The action gate locks the tiles only for the people in the fight (action-rolls.mjs:259), so the bystander pays the action, rolls, and the packet reaches resolveStageSix, where the same function runs on the GM with the whole cast, leaves the victim out and refuses. The bridge tells the roller 'You cannot frame that student.' and the step comes back. Nobody else the menu offers can be refused that way, so the refusal names the victim of an incident the bystander is kept out of.
findings.failure_scenario: While a murder runs in the Kitchen, a student elsewhere uses Tamper to frame a rival who happens to be its victim: after the roll they read 'You cannot frame that student.' and get their action back - and now know who is being killed, or already lies dead, before any body is found.
findings.expected: Who is in a running incident is kept from a bystander (incident-store.mjs:176-178; resource-guard.mjs:279-283 names this as E06's rule). The exclusion's own comment is about the killer: 'Framing the person lying dead in the room is a confession with extra steps' (cleanup.mjs:1587-1589).
findings.fix_sketch: On the GM, leave the victim out only for a roller who is in the incident's cast; let a bystander's trail at the victim stand like any other.
findings.refutation_tried: Checked that a bystander can act while an incident runs: the gate refuses the nine tiles for WHY.incident, which is the fight's sides only (action-rolls.mjs:133-134, 259-262), and remnants.mjs:379-386 treats a witness's Search during an incident as ordinary. Checked the other reasons the GM's list can differ from the menu's: itself, a Monokuma and the published dead are the same on both browsers (livingStudents is the table's fact, death.mjs:23-25), so only the victim differs - or a student published dead while the dice were in the air. After the close murderState is null on the GM and the victim is listed again, so the window is the running incident. The refusal and the give-back are deliberate for the killer's road (E03, S05-40; E09 fix r2-G3).
findings.tests_near: Tier 2 'Stage 6's own refusals give the killer back the step they paid and no more' (scripts/tests-tier2.mjs:23260-23338) refuses the killer's trail at the killer themselves; no test sends a non-participant's trail at the victim.

findings.title: A Reroll puts an erased trace back hidden and unfound: its finders lose it from their maps and the row loses the find, the GM's words mark and the GM's band mark
findings.where: scripts/cleanup-reshape.mjs:101-138 (recreationDataFor keeps no hidden, foundAt, foundVia, incidentFound, gmEdited, gmBand); scripts/cleanup.mjs:2112-2127 (the put-back); scripts/remnants.mjs:535 and 651-654 (a placed trace is hidden, foundAt null)
findings.what_happens: A successful erase stores the trace's creation data in the receipt; a Reroll's undoLastCleanup places it again under its id with placeRemnant(data, { keepId: true }), which creates the token hidden (unless it is an incident's trace while its incident runs) and writes a fresh row with foundAt null. The receipt holds none of the found state, so a trace that had been found comes back hidden: visibility.mjs:713 leaves a hidden token to Foundry, and every holder of a copy stops seeing it. Nothing shows it to them again - mintFindCopy answers HELD for a holder before it reaches revealRemnantToFinder (observe.mjs:1104, 1149) - until a student with no copy finds it. The row also loses gmEdited (the next find whispers the GMs to describe a trace they already described) and gmBand. Through Tamper's door the eraser always holds a copy, so the roller is among those who lose it.

findings.title: Move the Body asks where the victim's walking token stands, not where the body lies
findings.where: scripts/cleanup.mjs:151-155 (bodyIsHere -> sameRoom(actor, victim)); scripts/movement.mjs:3647-3671 (locateActor answers a Monocub's walker unless asked for the body); scripts/cleanup.mjs:1970 (applyMoveBody then carries the corpse token)
findings.what_happens: bodyIsHere, asked on the killer's browser before Move the Body is paid and on the GM before it is resolved, compares the killer's room with locateActor(victim). For a victim who has become a Monocub that is the token it walks (walkerOrBody, body = false). applyMoveBody was taught the difference in the E62 C3b fix and picks the corpse (`!isCubToken(t)`), but its reach is still computed from the killer's room. So with the Monocub standing beside the killer the check passes and the corpse is teleported from wherever it lies on that scene into a room next to the killer; with the corpse beside the killer and the Monocub elsewhere the action is refused as 'the body is not here'. The other readers of a body's place ask for the body (events.mjs:625, body-tile.mjs:158).
findings.failure_scenario: The GM leaves Stage 6 open after the discovery and makes the victim a Monocub; the Monocub walks into the killer's room, the killer's Move the Body succeeds, and the corpse jumps from the far side of the school into the room next door.
findings.expected: scripts/cleanup.mjs:143-149: 'A body that cannot be placed is not here, and the action is refused before it is paid for'; movement.mjs:3661-3665: 'where it stands is the token it walks, where its body lies the other. `body` asks for the body'.
findings.fix_sketch: Compare the killer's place with locateActor(victim, { body: true }) (or body-tile.mjs bodyPlaceOf) in bodyIsHere.
findings.refutation_tried: Read sameRoom and locateActor: no `body` is passed. A plain Spectator is another actor (spectator-dead.mjs), so only a Monocub victim has two tokens of the victim's actor. Not established: whether a GM can or does make the victim a Monocub while that incident is still open in Stage 6 - monocub.mjs has no test of the incident's state that I found, and the discovery can come while Stage 6 is open (destroyCleaningTools reads the running incident's killers, cleanup.mjs:2869-2872), but I did not trace the invitation's own conditions.
findings.tests_near: Tier 2 'Stage 6's own refusals ...' (23260-23338) and R3957 (bodyLanding) use a victim with one token; no test stands a Monocub victim in Stage 6.
findings.live_check: With Stage 6 still open after a discovery, make the victim a Monocub and walk it into the killer's room while the corpse lies in another; open the killer's Tamper menu and read whether Move the Body is offered, then roll it.

findings.title: The erase road's one `refused` answer is not passed on by the bridge's run: the asker is answered as done
findings.where: scripts/cleanup.mjs:1208-1211 (resolveCleanup answers { refused }); scripts/bridge-runs-acts.mjs:973 against 938 (the Stage 6 road passes its own on, the erase road does not)
findings.what_happens: resolveCleanup refuses an attempt through Tamper's door whose packet claims no step it may and for which the GM finds no action to take, and answers { refused: 'nothing was carried out: no action was left to pay for it' }. handleCleanup tests only `!cleaned` on that road, so the object is read as an answer, nothing is returned, and the bridge replies ok; the same refusal from resolveStageSix is passed on two branches above. An honest browser reaches it only if the killer's Stage 6 begins while their Tamper menu, opened before it, is still open: the menu keeps viaAction true (action-tamper.mjs:235, 257) while chargeTamper, asked later, takes the killer's Sanity step (tamperPriceSkip), which validPrice does not accept on that door - the Sanity is spent on the roller's browser and no card says why nothing happened.
findings.failure_scenario: A console's Tamper packet with no price and no action left is answered ok and told nothing; in the rare honest crossing above, a killer loses a Sanity mark to an attempt that silently did not happen.
findings.expected: The repository's trust-model rule file (trust-model.md), step 3 of 'How to add a bridge action': a run 'refuses by returning { refused: "<English reason>" }' and 'never answers a done for nothing'.
findings.fix_sketch: In handleCleanup, pass `cleaned.refused` on as the Stage 6 branch does.
findings.refutation_tried: Looked for an honest road that reaches line 1208 in ordinary play: the tile's browser pays an action and claims it (chargeTamper, payPrice with the Sanity step skipped), the killer's own Stage 6 says viaAction false, and the free attempt is taken before the test. How often the GM's HUD redraws the Event card that calls keyPlanStatus (events.mjs:642): each call walks every scene's traces and every living student's bullets.
